business_problem: Pearson needed to answer learner questions, returns, and order requests more intuitively as customer expectations shifted toward conversational support across chat and voice.
solution_summary: Pearson built a learner support layer on Agentforce to give students, teachers, and administrators self-service help across digital channels. The Pearson Virtual Assistant handles FAQs, returns, order tracking, invoices, and account questions in web and mobile chat, while Agentforce Voice extends the same experience to phone support. Requests are routed to specialized subagents that use trusted enterprise context rather than generic answers: Service Cloud stores the knowledge articles and support content, and Data 360 joins order and customer context so each interaction reflects the learner's current situation. For order-related questions, the assistant can also reach data held in Google BigQuery through zero-copy access. When a request falls outside the agent's scope, the conversation is handed to a human rep with the full context preserved so support continues without forcing the learner to start over.

solution_components.name: Agentforce
solution_components.role: Runs the AI agent workflows that answer learner questions, process returns, and track orders across chat and voice.

solution_components.name: Agentforce Voice
solution_components.role: Extends agentic support into voice channels used to answer learner questions, process returns, and track orders across chat and voice.

solution_components.name: Service Cloud
solution_components.role: Stores cases, knowledge, and service context that supports teams as they answer learner questions, process returns, and track orders across chat and voice.

solution_components.name: Data 360
solution_components.role: Unifies enterprise and behavioral data so teams can answer learner questions, process returns, and track orders across chat and voice with current context.

business_outcome: Pearson reported 225k questions answered since August 2025, 70% resolution in its UK Schools division, and a voice-support design expected to handle about 2,500 calls per month.
